hash_binding: Every span_sha256 is sha256 over the normalised span text read from git show <migration_candidate>:<file>; candidate_blobs records each per-file git_blob_sha1 and content_sha256.  The live worktree is not used for these hashes.
old_predicate: identity_match and the receipt's declared range covers the current census line; when current_census_line is unset the OLD tool falls back to the obligation's retained enumeration coordinate
normalisation: split on universal newlines (Python str.splitlines), rstrip() every line, join with '\n', sha256 over UTF-8 bytes (no trailing newline)
claim_scope: The span hash covers only the operation's own text and its attributes: from the first non-documentation attribute/qualifier line through the brace-matched closing brace. Documentation comments (///, //!, /** */) above the attributes are excluded. The hash does NOT cover dispatchers, shared guards, macro headers/invocations, caller closures, or any other code outside that span; those remain governed by the existing freeze and mechanism-scope rules. This is a narrowing claim, not a strengthening one.
